build: PAL, two-sided G64 pair supplied by the contributor (side 1 SHA-256 45e07b32..., side 2 7a402586...); EA loader, no crack or trainer

exclude: zero page: the Downhill Race's position, scroll, sprite and sound state, written at run time
not the Downhill Race's: neither its files nor its code write or read these bytes (simulator write and read maps from the hand-over and from play); left by earlier programs
run-time buffers: the two characters under each of the 35 flags, saved when a flag is knocked down ($161F, $162E) and put back by restore_flags ($1651)
mirror tables computed at start-up by build_mirror_tables ($1E48): $0700 reverses the 8 bits of a byte, $0600 reverses its four bit pairs; no byte of them is loaded
left by earlier loads after the load stub; the Downhill Race does not write or read them

inside file $1B between the note frequency table and load_file_numbers: an alternating $FF/$00 fill with a few stray bits, like uninitialised RAM saved with the file; no instruction reaches it (the table reads are indexed by a nibble or a slot offset) and the simulator never read it
the end of file $1B past the last variable ($3F82): an alternating $00/$FF fill with a few stray bits, like uninitialised RAM, that no code reads (simulator read map, opcode scan)
the tail of font file $23 (characters $FD-$FF) past the end of file $27; the status rows only use characters below $40 and nothing else reads it
four 64-byte sprite buffers (blocks $D0-$D3) that build_pose_sprites ($2760, $2A52) fills at run time from the pose shapes; no byte is loaded
three bytes between the end of file $26 ($7DFC) and file $1F ($7E00); not loaded, not read
forty bytes between the end of file $1F ($A5D7) and file $1E ($A600): not loaded and not read, identical to High Jump's memory
forty bytes between the end of file $1E ($CDD7) and the copy of file $1C ($CE00): not loaded and not read, identical to High Jump's memory
past the copy of file $1D: eight bytes the copy loop at $1E1B takes from beyond the file, then the tail of a RAM copy of the KERNAL from an earlier load; nothing reads them
stale bytes between the loader and the event manager, unchanged since the title; nothing refers to them
extra: font file $23, characters $00-$3F, shown in the status rows ($D018 = $40)
file $24: the eleven overlay sprites, blocks $08-$12
files $25 (the messages) and $27 (the sound-effect tables and scripts)
files $21 and $22: the riding sprites, blocks $50-$CF
file $26: the music (phrase table, scripts, phrase chooser code, note streams, phrase graph)
file $1F: the colour and terrain map, 255 rows of 40
file $1E: the character map, 255 rows of 40
files $1C and $1D copied under the I/O area: the pose directories and the pose shapes

comments.text: 6510 data-direction register. The Downhill Race never sets it; its only reference is init_race's zero-page clear at $1CBE, which starts at X = $13 and so never reaches it.

6510 processor port. init_race and the raster interrupt set $25 (RAM at $A000-$BFFF and $E000-$FFFF, I/O at $D000); load_files and the pose readers switch to $24 for the RAM under the I/O area ($1DD5, $27DE, $2823) and restore it.

The load stub, copied here by the resident event manager's run_load_stub ($FA58, template $F925) with this event's row of the load table: load file $1B to $0880 (load_file $F230, A = $1B, X/Y = $0880), mask interrupts, set CIA 1 port A to output and port B to input, select keyboard row $7F and jump to the event's entry at $0880. PRACTICE AGAIN re-runs only the final JMP $0880 ($F93E), so the event restarts without the disk.

Entry of the Downhill Race. On the first run these three bytes are JSR load_files ($1D7C), which loads files $1C-$27 and then overwrites them with three NOPs (EA), so a restart from the event manager's PRACTICE AGAIN (JMP $0880) skips the disk. Then init_race ($1CB6) sets everything up. In a competition ($FE11 = 0) the foot choice $3F82 is reset to regular; in practice it survives a restart because init_race clears the variables only up to $3F81. Any value of 2 or more is also reset. Then interrupts on and the main loop.
Operand of the JSR load_files at $0880 (low byte); load_files overwrites it with $EA ($1DB6) so the three bytes become NOPs after the first run.
High byte of the JSR load_files operand, also overwritten with $EA ($1DB9).

Main loop: game_frame ($0FEB, runs once per frame when the raster interrupt has set $3F66), handle_collisions ($1B3E), the two sideways-step checks ($2346 right, $2312 left), update_scroll_base ($22D4), game_frame again, check_finish ($0D20) and check_run_stop_commodore ($08B8), forever. The frame's other work happens in the raster interrupt.

Read keyboard row 7 (CIA 1 port A = $7F) and keep bits 7 (RUN/STOP) and 5 (Commodore key) of port B in $3F81; act only on a change. RUN/STOP pressed: $FE12 = $FF (quit), reset the sound driver and JMP $FE06 to the event manager, which goes to the shop. Commodore key pressed: flip $FE10 (sound off/on) and keep a copy in $3F80, which the interrupt's sound band uses to silence the driver. Same keys as High Jump's $1A08/$1A24.

The message on text row 2, column 10, colour 15. $3F39 negative (a fall, set at $253D): a random one of the eight taunts at $44C0 (NO POSERS, NO SNIVELERS ...); positive (points scored, $0CA7): a random one of the eight cheers at $4560 (RADICAL!, HANG LOOSE ...). Either stays $50 frames ($3F3A), then erase_message ($093F) prints 17 spaces. With nothing pending, while riding (state 0) and on a random 1 in 256 on frames where $3F0E bits 0-1 are clear, one of the eight exhortations at $4600 (DO A TRICK, GO SKATE ... SKATE OR DIE!).
Print the 17 spaces at $37E9 at the text cursor ($27 column, $28 row) set by the caller: clears a message.
Inside JSR random at $0952 (its high byte): the RESET vector in RAM ($FFFC) points here, left by earlier programs; the hardware never fetches it with RAM mapped.

State 5 (the start), fire: erase the CHOOSE CONTROL line (34 spaces on row 2) if it is showing ($3F7F), and if the push-off has not begun ($3F2D = 0) set $3F2D and start action 9, the push-off animation, through start_action ($0A1B).
State 5 (the start), any joystick direction before the push-off: count frames in $3F7E and every tenth frame flip the foot choice $3F82 (regular/goofy), then show the choice (start_idle).

State 5 (the start), no input; also the tail of start_direction. Until the push-off begins, print CHOOSE CONTROL : and REGULAR FOOT or GOOFY FOOT (pointers $3827/$3829 by $3F82) on row 2 in white. When no action is playing: after the push-off ($3F2D set) the race begins, speed $55 = 2, state 0, heading 8 (down and to the right), the skater moved one step right and two down; before it, start idle action 8 (1 in 16) or 7 at random.
Start the scripted action in $3F29 from its first frame ($3EF2 = 0, $3F2C = 0) with the pose anchored at x $82, y $5F ($3F2A/$3F2B), where the skater stands at the start line.

State 6, after the finish line, called through the control table. Phase $3F2E = 0: coast on until the skater is clear of the left side ($5C >= $1E) and above y $7B, or stopped; then turn the heading back to straight down one step a frame and, once straight, start action $0A (phase 1). Phase 1: when the action ends play action $0B and slow down one step; at speed 0 choose the final pose, $0E after three or more falls ($3F3C), $0C with a trick score of 40 or more, else $0D, and show the results (show_results $0B14); phase 2. Phase 2: wait for fire, then leave_event ($0D57).

Anchor the playing action's pose at the skater: x = 2 * $5C + $14 into $3F2A, y = $5D + $33 + a vertical offset from the action's frame ($3DEC indexes $3D75 by action, plus the frame $3EF2) into $3F2B, the offset also kept in $3F30.

End of the race: let the message timer and any pending points finish ($092D, $0CE0), then print the results on text row 2 in BCD with leading zeros suppressed ($1F07). Column 14, yellow: NO BONUS when the trick score $3EE5/$3EE6 is zero, else BONUS and the trick score followed by 00. The time score in $FE05/$FE04/$FE03 is zero from 1:30 on; under 1:30 $FE04 = $90 minus the time in seconds (BCD; minute 1 counts 60) and, when that is not zero, $FE03 = four times the tenths digit plus 1. The ADC at $0B9A has no CLC before it: in the first minute the carry left by the printing is set when the trick score is zero, so the time score is 100 lower. Column 0: SCORE: and the time score. Then the trick score is added to $FE04/$FE05 (so a trick point is worth 100) and column 28 shows TOTAL:. $FE03-$FE05 is what the event manager records. Simulated: 0:45.5 with no tricks gives 4421, with one trick point 4521 + 100 = 4621.

Add A (BCD) to the pending points $3EE9 and request sound $11 through $8B. Callers and amounts: 1 for landing facing the other way ($2E52) or after a jump off the rough-ground drop ($2E6D), 2 for a jump over a bench-like obstacle ($2E7C), for going up the skull ramp ($1482) or for bouncing off a wall in the air ($1BB5), 3 for entering the pipe ($142D) and $10 for leaving it ($1416), 4 for the roof ($173D) and the hurdles and the arch on the right ($1843, $18AB), $20 for two spins in one jump ($2E5E), and 5, $20, $40, $40 for successive jumps over water since the last fall ($2E3A, table $3ED5); a fifth and later water jump read on past the table ($4C, $80, $08, $07, $C3, $37, then zeros), and $4C is not a BCD number.
Clear the pending points $3EE9: the clock has passed 1:30.

Once a frame: points count only while the clock is under 1:30 (minutes $3EEF < 2, and below $30 seconds in minute 1), else they are discarded. New pending points ($3EE9) move to $3EEA; during a fall (state 4) they are thrown away; otherwise they are added to the trick score $3EE5/$3EE6 (BCD), a cheer is requested ($3F39 = 1) and they are shown as *nn* on text row 2, column 33, for $50 frames ($3EE8), then erased by printing the spaces at $37F4.

End the points display: clear the shown points $3EEA and its timer $3EE8 and print six spaces (the tail of the blank string, $37F4) in colour 0 at text row 2, column 33, over the *nn*. Also called by race_results before the results line.

Run from the sound band of the raster interrupt before each sound tick: the first time with the sound on ($FE10 = 0, $3F79 = 0) request sound 4, the music; then queue the sound ID left in $8B by the game (queue_sound_id $2FEA) and clear it. One request per tick, the last one written wins.

Main loop: when the skater has crossed the finish ($3F16, set by terrain_finish $12BD), clear the turning and spin state, end any action, switch to state 6 (end of race) and lower the skater to the ground. With no fall during the race ($3F34 = 0) add the five-point no-fall bonus (BCD 5) to the pending points.

Leave for the event manager: restore every knocked-down flag in the course map (restore_flags $1651), clear the music flags $3F79/$3F7A, mask interrupts, reset the sound driver and JMP $FE06. Reached by fire after the results ($0AED).

Put the skater back on its feet: clear the crouch sprite offsets (clear_crouch $2DDB), the action and fall state ($3F65, $3F33, $3F62-$3F64, $3F31/$3F32, the spin count $3F37), speed $55, heading, turning and spin rates, hiding under bridges ($3F02), height and ground level ($3F67/$3F69), the terrain under the skater ($3F6F-$3F74) and the eight sprite-hide flags $73-$7A; y $5D is held at $64 or above.

Each frame while riding (not in states 4 or 5 or the end of race; under a bridge, $3F02, it hides the skater instead, $0FAE): position the five riding sprites. x = 2 * $5C + $14 with the MSB bits in $83; the direction index $4A (0-15, from the heading $3EFE plus the spin $3EFC and the turn $3EFA) and $4C (+16 when crouched, $60) select x offsets from $382B/$384B/$386B (body sprites $87, +1, +2) and $389B (board and shadow, $89 and +1), y offsets from $388B/$38BB/$38DB plus the crouch offsets $394A-$394E and the height $3F69 over the ground $3F67. Colours 8, 1 and 6 for the body, the skater's attribute $FE02 for the board, 0 for the shadow. Sprite pointers: a bank from $393F-$3947 chosen by the crouch selectors $393A-$393E, plus the direction. Sprites flagged in $73-$7A are hidden (x = 0) and the flags cleared.
Under a bridge or in a tunnel ($3F02): park the three body sprites and the board at x 0, or at $18 for obstacle class 5, and clear their MSB bits; the shadow too unless $3F65 says it stays.

The game's frame, run from the main loop when the raster interrupt has set $3F66: ground level from the terrain (update_ground_level $1916), terrain effects (apply_terrain $126A), place_skater_sprites, spins (apply_spin $10FF), read the map under the skater (read_terrain $1C29), the joystick (read_joystick $2B34), height and jumping (update_height $1A6C), steering (update_velocity $19F0), the scroll speed limit ($124E), animated characters ($115C), the clock (update_clock $1060), the status line ($1C95), messages ($08E6) and points ($0C5B). Clears $3F66.
Add three seconds to the clock (BCD) and clear the request $3F61, unless the clock already reads 9:57 or more, which is then held at 9:59. Requested when the skater lands in water (action 6, $25FF).

Run the race clock while $3EF0 is set: tenths $3EED every 6 frames, seconds $3EEE (BCD) every ten tenths, minutes $3EEF every 60 seconds, held at 9:59.9. Six frames a tenth is right for a 60 Hz machine; on a PAL C64 a game second lasts 1.2 real seconds. Apply a pending water penalty first. Print TIME m:ss:t at row 1, column 28 in white.
Print a colon at the text cursor.

While riding (state 0) with a spin rate $3EFC (set by fire + left/right, $2BBD/$2BFC): turn the heading |rate|/8 + 1 steps in the spin's direction through steer_step ($192B, with the turn input $3EFA forced to +1 or -1 and restored after), losing speed at each step (slow_down $2E88), and decay the rate by one toward zero each time the heading actually moves.

Animate the course's characters in the charset at $4800, each on a random chance: 1 in 16, flip two pixel pairs of characters $E3/$E4 ($4F1F, $4F27), the skull's eyes on the ramp; 1 in 16, swap characters $EA/$EB ($4F50-$4F5F) between the two frames at $3C35/$3C3D ($3EC3 toggles), the skull's jaw; 1 in 8, step $3EC4 through four frames of the flag cloth, copying 8 bytes each from $3C46/$3C66/$3C86/$3CA6 into flag characters $81, $86, $87 and $89 ($4C08, $4C30, $4C38, $4C48) and the first column into the overlay flag sprite (block $0C, $4301 + 3n); then three times, 1 in 16, move one of the three bobbing objects in the lake (characters $F8-$FA, $4FC0-$4FD7) a pixel up or down within its cell ($3EBA/$3EBD offsets, $3EC0 direction).

Pseudo-random byte in A: (seed_lo >> 2) - seed_lo, using the caller's carry, shifted right; its carry is rotated into $3F0E and $3F0D is rotated right; returns $3F0D EOR $3F0E. The same generator as the music's phrase chooser ($760B) and High Jump's.

Set $3F07, the number of scrolled pixels per step of height on a ramp (terrain_ramp $146D), from the map row at the top of the screen $21: 6 above row $50 (the skull ramp), 2 from $50 to $A7, 4 from $A8 on (the steps by the building).

Run the terrain handlers for the three map cells under the skater (read_terrain): the middle cell's type $3F73 through the 16-entry table $3B5E, then the left ($3F72) and right ($3F74) cells through $3B7E, whose first ten entries do nothing. Each handler's address is written into a JSR here ($1290, $12A5, $12BA). Hides the overlay sprites first.
Operand of the JSR at $128F: the middle cell's terrain handler, written from $3B5E by type ($1285/$128C). The snapshot holds $1468.
High byte of the middle-cell handler's address.
Operand of the JSR at $12A4: the left cell's handler from $3B7E.
High byte of the left-cell handler's address.
Operand of the JSR at $12B9: the right cell's handler from $3B7E.
High byte of the right-cell handler's address.
Terrain handler that does nothing: side cells of types 0-9 and $F.

Terrain type 9, the start and finish lines and the lake's islands: unless falling (state 4) or finished (6), keep the clock running ($3EF0 = 1), so the clock starts when the skater first rolls onto the start line. With the scroll at $0730 or more ($24 = 7, $23 >= $30) stop the clock and set $3F16, the finish (check_finish $0D20).
Terrain type 4, rocks and bushes: mark the jump for a point ($3F62, scored on landing) and fall unless the skater is at least 7 above the ground (fall_if_low).
Fall (start_fall) unless the height $3F69 is at least 7 above the ground level $3F67.

Start a fall unless one is playing ($3EF1): sound 3, keep the shadow sprite unless the skater was hiding ($3F65), count the fall in $3F3C (three or more choose the losing pose at the end). Action 1 when the skater was heading within 4 steps of straight down or nearly sideways; otherwise action 2 or 3 by the side the skater is heading and whether it rides backwards ($3F14), action 3 drawn mirrored ($3D = 1).
Start fall action 4, or 5 when riding backwards ($3F14), unless a fall is playing: a crash into an obstacle (pipe lip, walls, hurdle 2).
Terrain type 5, water: on the ground (height = ground level) fall, which becomes the splash (action 6, $25DF); in the air, flag the jump as over water ($3F32) for the water points on landing ($2E2C).

Terrain type D, the top of the big pipe (rows $79-$7C): from row $7C on, fall (start_fall_alt) unless ducking ($3F06); inside the pipe ($3F02) go on as terrain_pipe; otherwise draw the pipe's end over the skater with overlay sprites 8 and 9 ($88 and $88+1) at x $48/$60 and hide the board and shadow behind it.
Enable the two overlay sprites Y and Y+1 in the enable mask $85 and the multicolour mask $86.
Terrain type E, the mouth of the big pipe: leave the pipe ($3F02 = 0), draw the mouth over the skater with overlay sprites $0A/$0B at x $48/$60, and once per passage ($3F33) score $10 for coming out.

Terrain type F, inside the big pipe. On entering ($3F33 clear) score 3. Centre the skater on the pipe (x $1D) and point it straight down (heading 0, or $20 riding backwards). Unless falling: ducking ($3F06) hides all eight sprites ($73-$7A) and sets $3F02, inside the pipe; not ducking crashes (start_fall_alt).
Terrain types 0 and $A in the middle cell, and $A at the sides: nothing to do but clear the obstacle class $62.

Terrain types 1-3, the skull ramp and the building's steps: once, score 2 ($3F35); reset the spin count; then for each pixel the course has scrolled since last frame ($3F11 against $25), while the middle cell is a ramp ($3F6E), count to $3F07 and raise the ground level $3F67 and the height $3F69 by one, losing a little speed. Rolling up the ramp lifts the skater; at its end the ground drops back to 0 (update_ground_level) and it is in the air.

Terrain type B, a flag: find which of the 35 flags (rows $3B9E, columns $3BC1) is within 2 rows and 4 columns. A flag already down ($3F3D,x) is ignored. If the skater's feet are in the flag's cell (fine-scroll and y tests), knock it down (knock_flag $1574); otherwise draw the flag as overlay sprite $0C in front of or around the skater ($1522) so it hides the right parts.
Show flag X as overlay sprite $0C (colour $0C) at its screen position, computed from its row and column and the scroll ($21, $1F), x MSB set for columns from $1C, obstacle class 3.

Knock flag X down: lose two steps of speed (one at speed 1), mark it ($3F3D,x), request a redraw ($52), and rewrite its cells in the course map at $A600 (row $3B9E,x, column $3BC1,x): the pole's characters go through flag_down_char ($163B), the cloth cell's character and colour are swapped with $3BE4,x, and the two cells below become the fallen flag ($FB/$FC, or $FD/$FE for a left-facing flag, $3C07,x) in the flag's colour, the old characters saved at $05BA,x and $05DD,x for restore_flags.
Character A of a standing flag ($80-$8A) to the one drawn when it is down, from $3C2A; any other character is returned unchanged. Preserves X.

Stand every knocked-down flag up again before leaving the event: for flags 34 down to 0 with $3F3D,x set, clear the mark and write the standing flag's characters ($80-$8A, choosing pole or edge pieces by what is around them), its colour byte ($3BE4,x swapped back) and the two saved cells ($05BA,x, $05DD,x) back into the course maps. The map is the loaded file, so without this a restart from PRACTICE AGAIN would find the flags down.
Terrain type 6, the roof of the building: once, score 4 ($3F64); the ground level becomes 7, so the skater rides on the roof.
Terrain type 7, grass: on the ground, slow down (slow_down $2E88) on every other frame, again when the speed is 8 or more, and again on every fifth frame; in the air nothing.
Terrain type 8, the low obstacles on rows $84-$88: flag the jump for 2 points on landing ($3F63); on the ground slow down as on grass and fall.

Terrain type C, four fixed objects chosen by the row under the skater $3F08: hurdle 1 (below $58), hurdle 2 ($58-$6F), the kicker on the right ($70-$9F) and the building (from $A0, object_building $18BA). A hurdle is drawn with overlay sprites $0D/$0E (its bar coloured from $3ED1/$3ED3 into sprite blocks $0D/$0E) and checked on its own row $3EC9,x when the fine scroll is below 2: hurdle 1 must be jumped, at least 6 high, or the skater stops and falls (action 1); hurdle 2 must be ducked under ($3F06), or the skater stops and crashes (start_fall_alt); passing either scores 4 once ($3F36). The arch uses sprites $0F/$10, scores 4 when crossed at least 6 high and needs at least 7 (fall_if_low).

Object 3 of terrain type C, the building at the left from row $A0: overlay sprites $11 at x $18 cover the skater; from row $AB the ground level is 7 (the roof's height); from row $B7 sprite 0 is the second overlay, pointer $12, x $18.
When the middle cell is not part of a ramp (type 0 or 4 and above), the ground level $3F67 drops to 0 and the ramp counters $3F35/$3F6D are cleared.

Turn by the turn input $3EFA: add it to the accumulator $59; each time |$59| reaches the threshold for the speed ($3970,$55: 2 when slow up to $0A at speed $13), take the threshold off and move the heading $3EFE one step (wrapping $20 to $E0), then check the 90 degree limits ($198A, $19BD) and update the spin state ($2B95). Leaves |heading| in $3EFF. The faster the skater, the slower it turns.

After a step to the right: at heading $11 (past sideways) riding forwards, lose two steps of speed and step back, unless already stopped, when the skater turns round ($3F14 flips, spin count +1). At $F0 riding backwards the same from the other side.
After a step to the left: the mirror of limit_turn_right, at headings $EF and $10.

Steer (steer_step), then split the speed by the heading: the sideways component from $394F,|heading| (0-15 forward, a reversed sign past sideways), times the speed $55, plus the fraction $3F13, over 16, goes to $5B and, signed by the heading, to the sideways step $58. scroll_and_move ($2051) uses speed - $5B as the downhill step.

Height and gravity. In states 2 and 3 (crouch and landing) nothing. State 1 (in the air): if the height has come within 9 of the ground, set it to ground + 9 and go to landing (state 3). Otherwise when the height is above the ground the skater is in the air (state 1, or still 4 when falling): add the vertical speed $3F6A to the fraction $3F6C and move the height one per 16, the speed growing by 1 each step (gravity). On the ground: height = ground, vertical speed 1, sprites reset; state 1 becomes 3, landing.
Sprite roles while riding: $88 = 1 (overlay sprites 1 and 2), $87 = 3 (body sprites 3-5), $89 = 6 (board 6 and shadow 7).
Collision flag $3F05 (a side wall of the ramp or the right edge): clear it and fall.
Collision flag $3F04 (a wall cell, type $A, under 14 high): sound $0C; fall (start_fall) from row $A0 on, otherwise crash (start_fall_alt).

Main loop: act on the flags the movement left. $3F03 (bounced off a wall at the side): bounce ($1B9F). $3F05: hit_wall_fall. $3F04: hit_low_wall. $3F15 (landed in the middle of a spin, set at $2E23): at speed 2 or more fall; slower, accept the spin as the new heading ($3EFE + $3EFC), turning round if it passed sideways (twice $2C1E), and set the facing $3F14 by the result.

Bounce off a wall at the side (types $A, under 14 high): sound $0C; in the air reverse the heading and score 2; on the ground reverse it too, except inside the pipe, where the skater is set straight down ($00, or $20 backwards).
RTS: the control table's entry for falling (state 4) and for impossible joystick values.
Map row $16/$17 (with $3C added after the first doubling) times 40: $12/$13 = the address in the character map $A600, $14/$15 = the same cell in the colour and terrain map $7E00.

Find the map row under the skater, ($23/$24 scroll - ground level, in $25/$26, + y $5D, capped at $9B) / 8, into $3F08, and for column $5C/4 read three cells: their characters into $3F6F-$3F71 and the high nibbles of their colour-map bytes, the terrain types, into $3F72 (left), $3F73 (middle) and $3F74 (right).
Clear the three text rows (clear_status_rows), print SKATER: and the name (draw_skater_name) and the clock (update_clock).
Fill the first 120 bytes of the screen at $5000 (text rows 0-2) with spaces.
Row 1, column 0, colour 15: SKATER: ($37C9) and the name the event manager left at ($FE00) (PRACTICE in practice).

Set up a race (every entry to $0880): save three video registers (save_video_registers, never read back), zero $13-$FF and the variables $3EE5-$3F81, fill the screen with spaces, set the sprite roles, put the skater at the start (x $3A, y $2D), VIC bank 1 ($DD00) with screen $5000 and the course charset $4800 ($D018 = $42), state 5 (the start), all sprites off and black-and-grey multicolours, the raster interrupt (install_raster_irq), $01 = $25, the IRQ vector at $FFFE to raster_irq ($1F47), the mirror tables (build_mirror_tables), the status rows (draw_status) and finally reset the sound driver.
Skater at the start line: x $5C = $3A, y $5D = $2D.

First entry only (called from the JSR that $0880 holds in the file): with $01 = $25 load the twelve files listed at $3787 (numbers $1C-$27) to the addresses at $3793/$379F through the resident loader ($F230). Files $1C and $1D both load at $8000 and are moved at once under the I/O area (copy_poses_under_io after the first, copy_shapes_under_io after the second), before file $1F lands on $7E00-$A5D7. Then write three NOPs over $0880-$0882 so a restart skips this.
Copy file $1C, the pose directory, from $8000 to $CE00-$D5FF (8 pages; the file is $768 bytes, so $CE00-$D567 is what counts) with $01 = $24, which puts RAM at $D000-$DFFF.

Copy file $1D, the pose shapes, from $8000 to $D568-$F198 ($1C pages and $31 bytes; the file is $1C29 bytes, so the last eight copied are not the file's) with $01 = $24. It starts where file $1C ends, so the two make one block.
Fill the screen $5000-$53FF with spaces ($20).
Build the tables used to draw a pose facing the other way: $0700,x = x with its eight bits reversed (hires sprites), $0600,x = x with its four bit pairs reversed (multicolour sprites).
Save $D018, $DD00 and $D021 in $3EE2-$3EE4. Nothing in the Downhill Race reads them back.
Mask CIA 1 interrupts and acknowledge them, wait for the raster to wrap, set the raster compare to line $FB (bit 8 clear) and enable the raster interrupt, then wait for the raster to wrap again.
Wait until the raster line changes to a value below 128: synchronises with the top of the screen.
Put screen code A at text column $27, row $28 of the screen ($5000 + row * 40, rows from $3B0C/$3B25) with colour $3F38 in colour RAM, and advance $27. Preserves Y.
Print the zero-terminated ASCII string at ($12) with A as its high byte: letters $41-$5A become screen codes 1-26, other bytes are printed as they are (space, digits, colon). Preserves Y.
Second entry of print_string with the whole address already in $12/$13 (the messages, from update_message $090B).

Print the BCD byte in A as two digits from $3B4E. Leading zeros are suppressed while $3F18 and $3F17 are both 0: $3F18 = 0 with A = 0 prints nothing; $3F17 = 0 drops a zero first digit. Callers set the two flags per field. Preserves Y.

Raster interrupt: save the registers and $01, set $01 = $25, acknowledge the VIC, then for the current band $36 patch the JSR at $1F78 with the handler from $37B3 (words), move $36 to the next band ($37BF) and set the raster compare to its line ($37BB). Interrupts are enabled again before the handler runs, so the next band can interrupt a long one. Four bands: $1F84 at line $F6, $1FF2 at $45, $1FC4 at $4D, $2019 at $5A.
Operand of the JSR at $1F78: the current band's handler, written from $37B3 by band number $36 at $1F61 (low byte). The interrupt re-enables interrupts (CLI, $1F77) before calling it.
High byte of the band handler's address ($1F67).

Band 0, raster line $F6 (bottom border): set up the status rows for the next frame (single-colour text, 38 columns, vertical scroll 0, $D018 = $40: screen $5000 and the font at $4000, background 6, blue) and, unless the previous run is still busy ($8D), run the frame's display work: the fall animation (update_fall $252B), the overlay sprites (place_overlays $23A9), the scripted actions (update_action $29D6) and the sprite registers (write_sprite_registers $237C), then set $3F66 so the main loop runs game_frame.

Band 2, raster line $4D: wait a time from $37AB that depends on the fine scroll $3EF7, so the switch lands at the start of the course, then background grey ($0C), multicolours $0F and $0B, $D018 = $42 (charset $4800), extended colour mode off and multicolour on with 40 columns.

Band 1, raster line $45, just below the three text rows: after eight NOPs turn on multicolour with the horizontal scroll $1E and set the vertical scroll $1F with extended colour mode on: an invalid mode that shows black, hiding the rows where the scroll changes until band 2 switches it off. Keep the fine scroll in $3EF7 for band 2 and move the course (scroll_and_move $2051).

Band 3, raster line $5A: count a frame in $8A. If the coarse scroll changed ($52) and no redraw is pending, redraw the course (redraw_course $20A5). Otherwise, unless already inside ($8C), run the sound for each counted frame: when the Commodore key has turned the sound off ($3F80) silence the driver once (init_sound_driver) and clear the music flag $3F79; then request_pending_sound ($0CFF) and update_sid_voices ($3021).

Move the skater and the course, once a frame except while falling: the downhill step speed - sideways ($55 - $5B, not below 0) is added to the fraction $53; each time it passes 8 the course advances a line (advance_course $2279). Then the coarse scroll is recomputed (update_coarse_scroll $22E3) and the sideways step $58 is added to $54; each time it passes 11 one way or the other, a step right ($5F) or left ($5E) is flagged for the main loop.

Redraw the 22 course rows of the screen (text rows 3-24) from the maps at the coarse scroll row $21: characters from $A600 + row * 40 to $5078 onwards, colour bytes from $7E00 + row * 40 to colour RAM $D878 onwards (colour RAM keeps the low nibble, the colour; the high nibble is the terrain type). Two rows per pass, each row in two halves of 20 columns, by self-modified absolute addresses ($2197-$21C5), eleven passes; clears $52 and the pending flag $3F1E at the end.
Low byte of the source of LDA $2196: the character map ($A600 + row * 40), the pass's first row, left half, columns 0-19, indexed by Y; redraw_course rewrites it for each pass.
High byte of the source address of LDA $2196 (the character map ($A600 + row * 40), first row, left half).
Low byte of the destination of STA $2199: the screen row, the pass's first row, left half, columns 0-19, indexed by Y; redraw_course rewrites it for each pass.
High byte of the destination address of STA $2199 (the screen row, first row, left half).
Low byte of the source of LDA $219C: the colour and terrain map ($7E00 + row * 40), the pass's first row, left half, columns 0-19, indexed by Y; redraw_course rewrites it for each pass.
High byte of the source address of LDA $219C (the colour and terrain map ($7E00 + row * 40), first row, left half).
Low byte of the destination of STA $219F: colour RAM, the pass's first row, left half, columns 0-19, indexed by Y; redraw_course rewrites it for each pass.
High byte of the destination address of STA $219F (colour RAM, first row, left half).
Low byte of the source of LDA $21A2: the character map ($A600 + row * 40), the pass's second row, left half, columns 0-19, indexed by Y; redraw_course rewrites it for each pass.
High byte of the source address of LDA $21A2 (the character map ($A600 + row * 40), second row, left half).
Low byte of the destination of STA $21A5: the screen row, the pass's second row, left half, columns 0-19, indexed by Y; redraw_course rewrites it for each pass.
High byte of the destination address of STA $21A5 (the screen row, second row, left half).
Low byte of the source of LDA $21A8: the colour and terrain map ($7E00 + row * 40), the pass's second row, left half, columns 0-19, indexed by Y; redraw_course rewrites it for each pass.
High byte of the source address of LDA $21A8 (the colour and terrain map ($7E00 + row * 40), second row, left half).
Low byte of the destination of STA $21AB: colour RAM, the pass's second row, left half, columns 0-19, indexed by Y; redraw_course rewrites it for each pass.
High byte of the destination address of STA $21AB (colour RAM, second row, left half).
Low byte of the source of LDA $21AE: the character map ($A600 + row * 40), the pass's first row, right half, columns 20-39, indexed by X; redraw_course rewrites it for each pass.
High byte of the source address of LDA $21AE (the character map ($A600 + row * 40), first row, right half).
Low byte of the destination of STA $21B1: the screen row, the pass's first row, right half, columns 20-39, indexed by X; redraw_course rewrites it for each pass.
High byte of the destination address of STA $21B1 (the screen row, first row, right half).
Low byte of the source of LDA $21B4: the colour and terrain map ($7E00 + row * 40), the pass's first row, right half, columns 20-39, indexed by X; redraw_course rewrites it for each pass.
High byte of the source address of LDA $21B4 (the colour and terrain map ($7E00 + row * 40), first row, right half).
Low byte of the destination of STA $21B7: colour RAM, the pass's first row, right half, columns 20-39, indexed by X; redraw_course rewrites it for each pass.
High byte of the destination address of STA $21B7 (colour RAM, first row, right half).
Low byte of the source of LDA $21BA: the character map ($A600 + row * 40), the pass's second row, right half, columns 20-39, indexed by X; redraw_course rewrites it for each pass.
High byte of the source address of LDA $21BA (the character map ($A600 + row * 40), second row, right half).
Low byte of the destination of STA $21BD: the screen row, the pass's second row, right half, columns 20-39, indexed by X; redraw_course rewrites it for each pass.
High byte of the destination address of STA $21BD (the screen row, second row, right half).
Low byte of the source of LDA $21C0: the colour and terrain map ($7E00 + row * 40), the pass's second row, right half, columns 20-39, indexed by X; redraw_course rewrites it for each pass.
High byte of the source address of LDA $21C0 (the colour and terrain map ($7E00 + row * 40), second row, right half).
Low byte of the destination of STA $21C3: colour RAM, the pass's second row, right half, columns 20-39, indexed by X; redraw_course rewrites it for each pass.
High byte of the destination address of STA $21C3 (colour RAM, second row, right half).

One line of downhill progress: a wall cell (type $A) in the middle under 14 high flags a crash ($3F04). While the skater is above y $48 it moves down the screen; otherwise the course scrolls: $23/$24 + 1 while the clock runs ($3EF0), and at the end of the course ($0750) the skater moves down the screen to $A5 instead. Sets $3F6E when the middle cell is a ramp (types 0-3).
$25/$26 = the scroll position $23/$24 minus the ground level $3F67: the row read_terrain uses.
Coarse scroll row $21 = scroll / 8, fine scroll $1F = 7 - (scroll AND 7) for $D011; a change of $21 sets $52 to request a redraw.

A step left flagged by scroll_and_move ($5E): at the left edge ($5C = 0) fall; a left cell of type 3 (the ramp's left wall) sets $3F05 (fall), of type $A under 14 high sets $3F03 (bounce); otherwise x $5C - 1.
A step right ($5F): at x $98 fall; a right cell of type 2 (the ramp's right wall) sets $3F05, of type $A under 14 high $3F03; otherwise x $5C + 1.

Copy the sprite shadow tables to the VIC: x $63-$6A and y $6B-$72 to $D000-$D00F, pointers $7B-$82 to $53F8-$53FF (the screen's sprite pointers), x MSBs $83, enable $84, priority $85 ($D01B: behind the background) and multicolour $86.

Place the overlay sprites ($88, $88+1) for the obstacle class $62 the terrain handlers set: 1 the end of the big pipe, 2 its mouth (both hide whichever skater sprites are below the pipe's edge, $73-$7A), 5 the building, 4 the hurdles and the arch on the right (at their rows $3EC5,x); 3, a flag, was placed by draw_flag_overlay; 0 turns them off.

Run the fall animation while $3EF1 holds an action. On the first frame: state 4, a taunt ($3F39 = $FF), mark the race as having a fall ($3F34), remember the row, y and x where it began ($3F23, $3F20, $3F25), stop all movement and load the action's frame count ($3D66) and frame time ($3E48). Each frame: hide the riding sprites, slide the skater (fall_slide $26B8), build the pose (build_pose_sprites $2760); every $3E48 frames step the frame. At frame 6 play the fall sound (fall_sound $267B) and, in water (character $9B or type 5 except characters $D6/$D7), switch to action 6, the splash, with sound 5 and the three-second penalty ($3F61). At the last frame hold it (the splash loops its last four) and wait for fire, which puts the skater back on the course (respawn $28FF) riding, state 0.
Once per fall ($3F7D): request the sound for the terrain in the middle cell: 7 on the road (type 0), 8 on rough ground (4), $0A in the pipe (D-F), otherwise 6.

During a fall, on the first tick of each frame time: unless a wall cell (type $A) is under the skater, move x by the action's horizontal steps ($3E41 by action into $3DFB, plus the frame); at x 0 or $E0 and above clamp to 0 and flag $3F2F (the sprites are hidden). Pose x = 2x + $14 ($3F21). Unless hiding or at the scroll's end, move y by the vertical steps ($3DEC into $3D75); pose y = y + $32 - height ($3F22).

Build the four sprites of the falling skater's pose: frame $3EF2 of action $3EF1 gives a pose number ($3D57 by action, then $3CC6), and the action's directory ($3E57) under the I/O area gives four six-byte entries (pose * 24, or from $D8 further for poses of 10 and more). For each: read_pose_entry, copy_pose_shape to the buffers $7400/$7440/$7480/$74C0 (sprite blocks $D0-$D3), position_pose_sprite. Sprites flagged in $73-$7A are then hidden.

With $01 = $24: read the next six-byte pose entry at ($46),$1D: the shape's offset from $D568 into $40/$41, its length - 1 into X, the x offset ($3EF5, mirrored as -(dx - 1) when $3D is set), the y offset ($3EF6) and the colour ($3F24, low nibble).

With $01 = $24: copy the shape at ($40) into the 64-byte sprite buffer at ($48) and fill the rest with zeros. Mirrored ($3D): read each byte through the bit-pair reversing table $0600 (multicolour sprite) or the bit reversing table $0700 (hires) and store it at the mirrored position from $3E7B, which swaps the left and right bytes of each three-byte row; the table address is written into the LDA at $287B.

Operand of the LDA $FFFF,y at $287B: the bit-reversing table used for a mirrored shape, $0600 (bit pairs) when the sprite is multicolour ($86) or $0700 (single bits), written by copy_pose_shape at $2859-$286B.
High byte of the mirror table address: $06 or $07.

Place pose sprite $3A (sprites $87-$89 then $89+1): x = $3F21 + dx with the MSB, y = $3F22 + dy, pointer $D0 + n, colour $3F24. Hidden instead (hide_skater) while in the pipe, and parked at x 0 when $3F2F says the skater has gone off the side.

After a fall: put the skater back at the row, x and y where it began ($3F23, $3F25, $3F20) and look along that row of the terrain map ($7E00 + row * 40) for road (type 0): from the left edge when x was below $50, from the right edge otherwise, take the first stretch at least four cells wide (or column $0A/$1E if there is none) and set x to its middle. Then reset_after_fall.

Run the scripted action $3F29 (7 and 8 idling at the start, 9 the push-off, $0A and $0B slowing at the end, $0C-$0E the final poses): on its first frame load the frame count ($3D66) and time ($3E48); each frame hide the riding sprites, build the pose at $3F2A/$3F2B (build_action_sprites $2A52) and place the board (place_action_board $2AA2); every frame time step the frame, and end the action ($3F29 = 0) after the last.
Like build_pose_sprites, for the scripted action $3F29 with the pose anchored at $3F2A/$3F2B: four sprites into $7400-$74FF, never mirrored.

Place the board sprite ($89) during a scripted action: for action 7 it moves with the frame ($3E75/$3E77), for 8 and 9 it sits at a fixed offset ($3E76/$3E78), for $0A-$0E at $3E79/$3E7A, raised by the frame's offset $3F30. Pointer: the riding board for the direction ($3945 by $393D, +6 except for $0A-$0E); colour $FE02.

Read both joysticks (CIA 1 ports A and B ANDed, so port 1 or 2 works) and pick the control record from $3984: (direction bits * 2) + $16 with fire + $2C for goofy foot ($3F82). A goofy skater has up and down, and left and right, swapped. The record holds seven handlers, one per state $3EF9; the one for the current state is written into the JMP at $2B7E. Clears the crouch flags first.
Operand of the JMP at $2B7E (low byte): the handler for the current state, taken from the control record ($37/$38) at $2B75; the snapshot holds start_idle ($09B9).
High byte of the state handler's address, written at $2B7B.
Riding (state 0), no input: unless a spin is running ($3EFC), let the turn rate $3EFA return to straight (ease_turn $2B8A).
Move the turn input $3EFA back toward 0 through the left or right easing ($2BA0/$2BDF entered past their own input).
Wind down a spin: with a positive spin rate $3EFC take a step off it through spin_left ($2BBD), with a negative one add a step through spin_right ($2BFC); one call per frame brings it back toward 0.

Riding, joystick toward the skater's left (right for goofy): wind down any spin (end_spin_if_any), then step the turn input $3EFA toward -1: $3EFB counts down each frame and every fourth frame $3EFA drops by one, stopping at -1.

Fire + left: start or speed a spin to the left on the spot. The turn input is cleared and the spin rate $3EFC grows by one step each frame ($3EFD) to -$20; reaching it completes a turn (turn_round $2C1E).
Riding, joystick toward the skater's right: wind down any spin and step the turn input $3EFA toward +1, one step every four frames ($3EFB), stopping at +1.
Fire + right: spin to the right, the rate $3EFC growing to $20; reaching it completes a turn (turn_round).
A half turn completed: clear the spin rate, flip the facing $3F14 (forwards/backwards), count it in $3F37 (two in one jump score $20) and swing the heading by $20, wrapping.
Riding, joystick down (up for goofy): push. Ease the turn, then every eighth frame ($57) add one to the speed $55, up to $10.
The push of ride_down without easing the turn: one more step of speed each eight frames, up to $10.

Fire + up: jump. At map row $3F08 $8C-$94 with x $5C in $78-$87 (the arch on the right), or row $4C-$55 with x $68-$93 (hurdle 1), set $3F0F and the sprite roles $87/$88/$89 = 1, 4, 6, so the skater is drawn in front of the overlay. Then state 2 (crouch before takeoff): turn input, spin rate and crouch counter $61 cleared, takeoff flag $3F10 set, the facing $3F14 saved in $3EEB and the half-turn count $3F37 cleared.

State 2 (crouching to jump) and the jump's rise: each frame take crouch step $61/2 from the tables at $38FB-$3931 (crouch flag $60, sprite selectors $393A/$393C/$393E, y offsets $394A-$394E) and, every other frame, add $3931,x to the height $3F69. After nine steps the vertical speed is -3 ($3F6A = $FD) and the skater is in the air (state 1).
State 1 (in the air): keep the landing crouch counter at its top ($61 = $10); while the takeoff flag $3F10 is set hold the airborne pose (crouch flag, sprites, y offsets -1), otherwise clear_crouch.

State 3 (landing): clear the takeoff flag and step the crouch tables backwards from $61 = $10, taking $3931,x off the height every other frame. After 17 frames $61 runs out and the skater is down: state 0, height = ground level $3F67, vertical speed 1, $3F0F cleared, sprite roles reset ($1B13), $3F6C cleared, then the jump is scored (score_landing $2DF8) and the crouch cleared.
Clear the crouch flag $60, the sprite selectors $393A/$393C/$393E and the y offsets $394A-$394E: the plain riding sprites.

On landing: sound $0E on grass (type 7 in the middle cell), else $0F. A spin caught halfway ($3EFC between 4 and $1C either way) sets $3F15 for handle_collisions; one nearer a full turn completes it (turn_round). Then the points: a jump over water gives the next value from $3ED5 (5, $20, $40, $40, then the bytes after the table; $3F31 counts them, is reset only by a fall, $0D80, and is never limited), landing facing the other way at speed 2 or more gives 1, two half turns in the jump ($3F37) give $20, the drop off the rough ground ($3F62) 1 and a bench ($3F63) 2.
Riding, joystick up (down for goofy): brake. Ease the turn, then slow down.
Lose speed: every eight calls ($57 counting down from 8) take one from the speed $55, not below 0.
State 2 handler in the fire + down records ($3A72, $3A9C): during the first four crouch steps go on with crouch_step; after that, drop the jump and duck instead (state 0, duck).
Fire + down: duck. Sets $3F06 (needed for the pipe and hurdle 2), the crouch flag $60 and the ducking sprites ($393C/$393E = 1).
Brake (slow_down) and turn right (ride_right): the record for up + right, and for down + left on goofy foot.
Duck and turn right: the record for fire + up + right on regular foot and fire + down + left on goofy (record $3AD4). On regular foot fire + up alone jumps, so the diagonal ducks instead.
Brake and turn left: up + left, or down + right on goofy foot.
Duck and turn left: fire + up + left on regular foot, fire + down + right on goofy (record $3AF0).
Push (push $2C4D) and turn right: down + right, or up + left on goofy foot.
Push and turn left: down + left, or up + right on goofy foot.
In the air, fire + right: hold the airborne pose and spin right.
Crouching, fire + right: go on with the crouch and spin right.
Landing, fire + right: go on with the landing and spin right.
In the air, fire + left: hold the airborne pose and spin left.
Crouching, fire + left: go on with the crouch and spin left.
Landing, fire + left: go on with the landing and spin left.

Number of sound IDs waiting in pending_sound_ids ($2F6C), 0-16. queue_sound_id ($2FEA) appends while it is below $10 (a 17th request is dropped); update_sid_voices ($3021) drains it to zero each tick. Cleared with the rest of $2F10-$2F7B by init_sound_driver.

Lowest priority among the three slots (the one a new sound must equal or beat). Recomputed at $36A6-$36BF after each start; set to 0 when a slot finishes ($360E), so the next request always wins that free slot.
Slot offset (0, 2 or 4) of the slot holding sound_weakest_priority: where start_sound_on_weakest_slot ($366E) puts the next accepted sound. Set at $36C2 and, when a slot ends, at $3611.
The primary-script command byte being executed, saved by dispatch_sound_opcode ($308B). Handlers test its bit 7 (BIT $2F13) for the operand mode and op 7 re-reads its high nibble.
Low byte of the left-hand value for sound op 6 (compare): the slot's frequency, pulse width, sustain level, loop counter or a byte read from memory; $2F15 holds the high byte for 16-bit compares.
High byte of the 16-bit left-hand compare value (frequency or pulse width) for sound op 6, compared first at $33A2.
Low byte (or only byte) of the right-hand operand of sound op 6, fetched by $33BE/$33D1 from the script or through an address.
High byte of the right-hand operand for 16-bit compares in sound op 6 (set by $33D1).
Per-slot shadow of the SID frequency low byte, at $2F18/$2F1A/$2F1C for slot offsets 0/2/4 (voices 3/2/1). Written with every frequency change and read back by op 4 (add) and op 6 (compare).
Per-slot shadow of the SID frequency high byte, at $2F19/$2F1B/$2F1D for slot offsets 0/2/4; paired with slot_freq_lo.
Per-slot shadow of the SID pulse-width low byte, at $2F1E/$2F20/$2F22 for slot offsets 0/2/4; set by op 1 and note command $AD, added to by op 4, compared by op 6.
Per-slot shadow of the SID pulse-width high nibble, at $2F1F/$2F21/$2F23 for slot offsets 0/2/4.

Low byte of slot 0's call-stack base address (init_sound_driver stores $7C, so slot 0 nests at $2F7C); the three slots' base pointers are words at $2F24, $2F26, $2F28, read as $2F24,x at $32FD and $3615. Same layout as High Jump's driver, moved $0CF5 bytes higher.
High byte of slot 0's call-stack base ($2F), read as $2F25,x with the low byte at $2F24,x.
Low byte of slot 2's (SID voice 2's) call-stack base: init_sound_driver stores $8C, so slot 2 nests at $2F8C.
High byte of slot 2's call-stack base ($2F).
Low byte of slot 4's (SID voice 1's) call-stack base: init_sound_driver stores $9C, so slot 4 nests at $2F9C.
High byte of slot 4's call-stack base ($2F).

Four note durations per slot, $2F2A-$2F2D (slot 0), $2F2E-$2F31 (slot 2), $2F32-$2F35 (slot 4), indexed by slot*2 + bits 7-6 of a note byte. The chosen value goes to the slot's wait timer ($2F42,x). Loaded by op $97 and note command $5D.

Four gate lengths per slot, $2F36-$2F39, $2F3A-$2F3D, $2F3E-$2F41, chosen like slot_note_durations. Non-zero: the note sets the gate bit and the gate timer ($2F43,x); zero: the note changes pitch without re-gating. Loaded by op $A7 and note command $6D.

Per-slot wait timer at $2F42/$2F44/$2F46 (slot offsets 0/2/4): while non-zero update_sid_voices decrements it instead of reading the script; a value N set in one tick makes the slot read again N+1 ticks later (checked against SID writes in the simulator). Set by op 8, notes and note commands.

Per-slot gate timer at $2F43/$2F45/$2F47: when flag bit 5 is set it counts down each tick and, G+1 ticks after a value G was set, clears the gate bit (bit 0) of the voice's control register ($3052), starting the release. The shadow $2F4F,x keeps the gate bit.
Sound ID playing in each slot, at $2F48/$2F4A/$2F4C; 0 after the slot ends. stop_sound ($2FF8) searches it.
Per-slot flags at $2F49/$2F4B/$2F4D: 0 idle; bit 6 active (set to $40 at start); bit 5 gate timer running; bit 4 inside a script call (call stack non-empty); bit 7 paused (skipped by the updater).
Per-slot sustain level counter (low nibble used) at $2F4E/$2F50/$2F52: op $24 adds to it and writes it as the high nibble of the SID sustain/release register; op $26 compares it.
Per-slot shadow of the SID control register (waveform bits and gate) at $2F4F/$2F51/$2F53; the gate timer clears bit 0 from it, notes set bit 0.
Per-slot loop counter at $2F54/$2F56/$2F58: set by op $31, added to by op $34, compared by op $36, and decremented by the loop op $15 (jump while non-zero).

Priority of the sound in slot 0 (SID voice 3); the slots' priorities are at $2F55/$2F57/$2F59. Set from sound_priorities ($46C6) on start, cleared at end; compared at $36A6-$36BF to find the weakest slot.
Priority of the sound in slot 2 (SID voice 2), read directly at $36AB/$36B2 when finding the weakest slot.
Priority of the sound in slot 4 (SID voice 1), read directly at $36A8 when finding the weakest slot (slot 4 is the first candidate).
Per-slot shadow of the SID attack/decay register at $2F5A/$2F5C/$2F5E; set by op $41 and note command $8D.
Per-slot shadow of the SID sustain/release register at $2F5B/$2F5D/$2F5F; op $24 rewrites its high nibble from slot_sustain_level.

Bytes used on each slot's call stack at $2F60/$2F62/$2F64 (two per nested call); a call pushes the return pointer at stack base + depth, a return pops it. Cleared by silence_sound_slot ($35FD) but, unlike High Jump's driver, not by start_sound_on_slot ($367A): a sound that replaces one stopped inside a call starts with the old depth. Not range-checked: more than 8 nested calls would run into the next slot's stack.
Result of the slot's last op 6 compare at $2F61/$2F63/$2F65, as the processor's C and Z bits: 0 less, 1 greater, 3 equal. Tested by the conditional jumps of op 5 against $332A/$3330.

Per-slot octave shift at $2F66/$2F68/$2F6A: the number of right shifts applied to note frequencies before the note's own octave bits are added (note_frequency, $35D0). Set by op $B7 and note command $4D.
Sixteen-byte queue of requested sound IDs: queue_sound_id ($2FEA) appends while sound_pending_count is below $10; update_sid_voices starts them newest first and empties the queue each tick.

Three 16-byte call stacks for nested sound scripts, $2F7C (slot 0), $2F8C (slot 2), $2F9C (slot 4), addressed through slot_stack_ptr_lo/hi. Each call pushes a two-byte return address. Not cleared by init: the bytes here are whatever the file carried (the play snapshot shows return pointers into the music, $7592 and $75A4); 8 levels per slot.

Sound driver reset: zero the script pointers $02-$07 and all driver state $2F10-$2F7B, silence the three SID control registers, set volume $0F with no filter ($D418), and point the slots' call stacks at $2F7C/$2F8C/$2F9C. The same code as High Jump's $22B7 with its state moved to $2F10. Called at the end of start-up ($1D70), before each exit to the event manager ($08E0 RUN/STOP, $0D63 end of race) and at $203F when the Commodore key turns the sound off.

Request sound ID A: append it to pending_sound_ids unless 16 are already waiting (then the request is silently dropped). The game calls it once a frame from request_pending_sound ($0D18, the ID left in $8B) and sound op 2 calls it from scripts ($318E). Clobbers X.

Stop sound ID A wherever it plays: search slot_sound_id for slots 4, 2, 0 and, if found, silence that slot through $35FD with interrupts disabled. No caller in the Downhill Race (opcode scan of the program and its files): part of the shared driver.
Found: Y = the slot's SID register offset; silence the slot with IRQs masked.
Set slot A (0-2, doubled to the slot offset) to flags $80 so update_sid_voices skips it. It replaces all flags rather than setting bit 7. No caller in the Downhill Race.
Clear bit 7 of slot A's flags. After pause_sound_slot the flags are $80, so this leaves 0 (idle) and the slot does not resume. No caller in the Downhill Race.

One sound tick, called from the raster interrupt's last band (irq_band3_redraw_and_sound $2019) once for each frame counted in $8A, after request_pending_sound ($0CFF): start every queued ID (start_sound_on_weakest_slot), then for slots 4, 2, 0 (SID voices 1, 2, 3): skip if idle or paused; run the gate timer; if the wait timer is zero, execute script commands until a $00 byte (end of tick) or the slot ends. High Jump's $232C with its state moved.
Read the next byte of slot X's primary script through ($02,X) and advance the pointer; the Z flag reflects the byte (a $00 byte ends the tick at $306F).

Execute primary command A: save it in sound_command_byte, push the handler for its low nibble from $30A3/$30B3 (RTS trick), and enter it with A = high nibble. Bit 7 of the command is the operand-mode flag; bits 6-4 select the sub-operation.

High bytes of the 16 primary sound-op handlers minus one, indexed by the low nibble of the command: 0 end/return ($35F6), 1 set register ($30C3), 2 queue sound ($3187), 3 poke/wait ($3196), 4 add ($3201), 5 jump/loop/call ($3290), 6 compare ($3336), 7 note stream ($33EF), 8 wait ($35DE), 9 end, A call 6502 code ($363E), B-F end.
Low bytes of the 16 primary sound-op handlers minus one (paired with $30A3); RTS lands one byte higher, on the handler.

Op $x1, set a voice register, sub-op = bits 6-4: 0 frequency (2 bytes lo,hi), 1-2 pulse width (2), 3 loop counter (1), 4 attack/decay (1), 5 sustain/release (1), 6-7 control/waveform (1). Bit 7 clear: the value follows in the script; bit 7 set: a 2-byte address follows and the value is read from there. Writes the SID and the slot shadow.
Op $02: the next script byte is a sound ID to request through queue_sound_id (started at the next tick, by priority); X and Y preserved.

Op 3 with an address operand (2 bytes). Sub-op 1 ($13/$93), wait-until: compare memory at the address with a value (bit 7 set: a literal byte; clear: a byte read through a second address); if unequal, back the script up 4 bytes and end this slot's tick, so it retries next tick. Other sub-ops ($03/$83), poke: store a value there (bit 7 clear: literal; set: read through a second address).

Unequal: rewind the script by 4 (right for the literal form $93 aa aa vv; the address form is 5 bytes long, so it would resume on its second byte), drop the dispatcher's return and go to the next slot.

Op 4, add to a register, sub-op = bits 6-4: 0 frequency += 2-byte value (bit 7 set: value read through an address), 1 pulse width += 2 bytes, 2 sustain level += byte, rewrite sustain/release and set the gate bit (re-trigger), 3+ loop counter += byte. Writes the SID and the shadows; 16-bit adds wrap.

Op 5, script flow. Bit 7 clear: $05 jump to a 2-byte address; $15 decrement the loop counter, jump while non-zero, else skip the address; $25 call (push the return pointer on the slot's stack, set flag bit 4); $35 replace this slot's sound with the ID in the next byte; others end. Bit 7 set: conditional jump on the last compare, $85 equal, $95 less, $A5 not equal, $B5 greater, $C5 less or equal, $D5 greater or equal; $E5/$F5 end.
First accepted compare result for the conditional jumps $85-$D5 (index = bits 6-4): 3,0,1,1,0,1. A jump is taken when slot_compare_result equals this byte or the one at $3330.
Second accepted compare result for the conditional jumps (same index): 3,0,0,1,3,3. With $332A this gives equal, less, not equal (1 or 0), greater, less-or-equal (0 or 3), greater-or-equal (1 or 3).

Op 6, compare and keep the result in slot_compare_result, sub-op = bits 6-4: 0 frequency vs 2-byte operand, 1 pulse width vs 2 bytes, 2 sustain level vs byte, 3 loop counter vs byte, 7 the byte at a 2-byte address vs byte; others end the script. Bit 7 set: the operand is read through an address instead.
Bytes 2C A9 01: BIT $01A9 hides LDA #$01 at $33B8, the entry for 'greater' (result 1); entered at $33B7 it gives 0, 'less'.
Fetch op 6's one-byte right operand into sound_compare_right: the next script byte, or (command bit 7 set) the byte read through a 2-byte address.
Fetch op 6's two-byte right operand into sound_compare_right/_hi: two script bytes, or (command bit 7 set) the word read through a 2-byte address.

Op 7. Bit 7 clear ($07): play the next event of the slot's note stream at ($08,X): low nibble 0-C a note (frequency table index, 0 silent), bits 5-4 extra octave shift, bits 7-6 pick duration and gate length; $xD a note command (handler $34E6 by high nibble, next byte its argument); $0E call a primary-script subroutine at the next 2 bytes; else end. Bit 7 set: $87 set the stream pointer, $97 four durations, $A7 four gate lengths, $B7 octave shift.
Read the next byte of slot X's note stream through ($08,X) and advance that pointer.

Low bytes of the 11 note-stream command handlers, indexed by the high nibble of a $xD stream byte: 0 note+duration ($34F8), 1 frequency+duration, 2 note+duration+gate, 3 frequency+duration+gate, 4 octave shift, 5 durations, 6 gate lengths, 7 control, 8 attack/decay, 9 sustain/release, A pulse width ($35AA). $BD-$FD index past the table (no check).
High bytes of the 11 note-stream command handlers, paired with note_command_handlers_lo; read at $344C and jumped to through $0E/$0F.
Note command $0D: the argument is a note byte (low nibble note, bits 5-4 octave); the next stream byte is a literal duration for the wait timer. Sets the frequency without touching the gate.
Note command $1D: the argument and the next byte are a literal SID frequency (low, high); the next byte is the duration. No gate change.

Note command $2D: note byte argument, then a literal duration and gate length. It stores the gate length in the slot's gate timer ($2F43,x) but, unlike High Jump's version, does not set flag bit 5, so the timer only runs if a note or op $88 has already set it; it never sets the gate bit.
Note command $3D: literal frequency (argument = low, next = high), then duration and gate length, handled by the tail of note command $2D (the same caveat about flag bit 5).
Note command $4D: the argument becomes the slot's octave shift ($2F66,x); then the next stream event is played in the same tick.
Note command $5D: the argument and the next three stream bytes replace the slot's four note durations ($2F2A); then the next event is played.
Note command $6D: the argument and the next three stream bytes replace the slot's four gate lengths ($2F36); then the next event is played.
Note command $7D: write the argument to the voice's SID control register (waveform, gate) and its shadow, then play the next event.
Note command $8D: write the argument to the voice's attack/decay register and shadow, then play the next event.
Note command $9D: write the argument to the voice's sustain/release register and shadow, then play the next event.
Note command $AD: the argument and the next stream byte are the pulse width (low, high), written to the SID and shadows; then the next event is played.

Note number A (0-15) to frequency in $0E/$0F: read the top-octave value from note_freq_lo/hi and shift it right by (bits 5-4 of the note byte in $11) + the slot's octave shift. Used by notes and note commands $0D/$2D.

Op 8: the next byte is a wait. $08 N: set the slot's wait timer, so the script resumes N+1 ticks later (once a $00 has ended this tick). $88 G: set the gate timer instead and flag bit 5, so the gate is released G+1 ticks later while the script runs on.
Op 0/9/B-F (and every invalid sub-op): if the slot is inside a call (flag bit 4), pop the return pointer from its call stack and continue there; otherwise fall into silence_sound_slot.

End slot X: clear the voice's control register (gate off, no waveform), the slot's ID, flags, stack depth and priority, and make it the weakest slot (priority 0) for the next request. Y = the voice's SID register offset. Also called from stop_sound.
Op $0A: call the 6502 routine at the 2-byte address that follows, preserving X and Y. The music's two voice scripts use it to call $75AA and $75BD, the code in file $26 that picks the next phrase.
JMP ($000E): the indirect call made by sound_opA_call_code; returns to $364F when the called routine executes RTS.

Read a 2-byte address from slot X's script and return the byte there in A and the following byte in $11 (a little-endian word), with Y restored to the voice's SID register offset. The operand form used when a command's bit 7 selects it.

Start sound ID A if its priority (sound_priorities, $46C6) is at least sound_weakest_priority: replace the sound in slot sound_weakest_slot. Equal priority wins, so a new sound replaces an old one of the same rank.

Start sound ID Y with priority A on slot X: set the slot's priority and ID, its script pointer from sound_script_addresses ($46A0/$46B3, file $27), clear its wait and gate timers (not its stack depth), set flags $40, zero the voice's seven SID registers, then find the new weakest slot (slot 4 first, then 2, then 0) for sound_weakest_priority/slot. Also used by op $35.

SID register offset of each sound slot, read at even X only: $36C6 (slot 0) $0E = voice 3, $36C8 (slot 2) $07 = voice 2, $36CA (slot 4) $00 = voice 1. The odd bytes $36C7/$36C9 are never read as offsets.

Low bytes of the note frequency table, 16 entries indexed by the note's low nibble: 0 silence ($0000), 1-12 the twelve semitones A, A#, B, C ... G# of the top octave ($70C7 ... $D4E6), 13-15 zero. In NTSC SID units entry 1 is 1760 Hz (A6); on a PAL machine it plays about 0.65 semitone flat.

High bytes of the note frequency table ($00,$70,$77,$7E,$86,$8E,$96,$9F,$A8,$B3,$BD,$C8,$D4,0,0,0); each step is a factor of about 1.0595, one semitone. note_frequency shifts the value right once per octave down.
File numbers load_files ($1D7C) loads in order: $1C-$27, twelve files.
Load address low bytes, one per file of $3787.

Load address high bytes: $1C and $1D to $8000 (copied under the I/O area to $CE00 and $D568 afterwards), $1E $A600, $1F $7E00, $20 $4800, $21 $5400, $22 $6800, $23 $4000, $24 $4200, $25 $44C0, $26 $7500, $27 $46A0.
Delay loop counts for the course band (irq_band_course $1FC4) by fine scroll 0-7: $0B for 0-4, $03 for 5-7, so the mode switch lands on the course's first pixel row.
The raster interrupt's four band handlers ($1F84 status, $1FF2 scroll blank, $1FC4 course, $2019 redraw and sound).
irq_band_handlers + 1: the handlers' high bytes ($1F64).
Raster line of each band: $F6, $45, $4D, $5A.
Next band after each band: 1, 2, 3, 0.

Zero-terminated texts for print_string ($1EE7, address low in $12, high in A), in ASCII capitals that print_string turns into screen codes 1-26: TIME at $37C3, SKATER: $37C9, NO BONUS $37D1 (BONUS is printed from $37D4, inside it), TOTAL: $37DB, SCORE: $37E2, seventeen spaces $37E9 (erase a message; the last six, from $37F4, erase the points), REGULAR FOOT $37FB, GOOFY FOOT $3808, CHOOSE CONTROL : $3815.
Low bytes of the foot texts by $3F82: REGULAR FOOT $37FB, GOOFY FOOT $3808.
High bytes of the foot texts.
x offset of the first body sprite ($87) by direction index $4A: 32 entries, the second 16 for the crouched poses.
x offset of the second body sprite ($87+1) by $4A (32 entries).
x offset of the third body sprite ($87+2) by $4C (32 entries).
y offset of the first two body sprites by $4A: 16 entries here; the crouched indices 16-31 read on into $389B.
x offset of the board and shadow sprites ($89, $89+1) by $4C (32 entries); its first 16 also serve as the crouched y offsets of $388B.
y offset of the third body sprite, and of the shadow, by $4C (32 entries).
y offset of the board sprite by $4C (32 entries).
The jump crouch, nine steps (index $61/2) read by crouch_step and landing_step: the crouch flag $60 for each step.
Crouch steps: the bank selector of body sprite 0 ($393A).
Crouch steps: the bank selector of body sprite 2 ($393C).
Crouch steps: the bank selector of the shadow ($393E).
Crouch steps: y offset of body sprites 0 and 1 ($394A/$394B).
Crouch steps: y offset of body sprite 2, the board and the shadow ($394C-$394E).
Crouch steps: height added on every other frame of the rise (and taken off again when landing).

Bank selectors of the five riding sprites ($393A-$393E: body 0, 1, 2, board, shadow): 0 picks the normal bank of the pair in $393F-$3948, 1 the crouched or ducking one. Written by the crouch handlers, duck and clear_crouch.
Bank selector of body sprite 1 (stays 0: nothing writes it).
Bank selector of body sprite 2.
Bank selector of the board (stays 0: nothing writes it).
Bank selector of the shadow.
Sprite pointer bases, pairs (normal, crouched) for each riding sprite, added to the direction: body 0 $50/$A0.
Board: $80/$80 (place_action_board adds 6).
Shadow: $90/$C0; the byte after the pair, $3949 = $80, is not read.
y offsets added to the five riding sprites while crouching ($394A-$394E), from the crouch step tables.
Crouch y offset of body sprite 1.
Crouch y offset of body sprite 2.
Crouch y offset of the board.
Crouch y offset of the shadow.

Speed split by |heading| 0-$20 (33 entries), read by update_velocity: 0, 1 ... $0F, then $0A at exactly sideways ($10) where the pattern would give $10, then -$0F ... -1, 0. The $0A breaks the run; whether it is deliberate is not known.
Turn threshold by speed 0-$13 (steer_step): 2 at a standstill up to $0A at the top, so a fast skater turns more slowly.

Control record pointers, 49 words, indexed by the stick's four direction bits * 2, + $16 with fire, + $2C on goofy foot (read_joystick $2B34). Fire entries for impossible stick values (up and down together) share slots with real directions without fire; every unused slot points at the empty record $3AFE.
control_records + 1: read_joystick takes each record pointer's high byte from here ($2B69).
Control record pointers for goofy foot with fire held ($3984 + $2C + $16 + direction * 2): up and down swapped, as in the goofy entries without fire before them.
Control record, no direction: seven handlers by state 0-6 (ride, air, crouch, landing, fall, start, end).
Record: down on regular foot, up on goofy: push.
Record: up (goofy: down): brake.
Record: right (goofy: left): turn right.
Record: left (goofy: right): turn left.
Record: down + right (goofy: up + left).
Record: up + right (goofy: down + left).
Record: down + left (goofy: up + right).
Record: up + left (goofy: down + right).
Record: fire alone: as no direction, but the start handler pushes off (start_fire).
Record: fire + down on regular foot: duck.
Record: fire + up on regular foot: jump.
Record: fire + up on goofy foot: jump too; fire + up and fire + down are the only directions goofy foot does not swap.
Record: fire + down on goofy foot: duck.
Record: fire + right (goofy: fire + left): spin right, in every riding and air state.
Record: fire + left (goofy: fire + right): spin left.
Record: fire + down + right (goofy: fire + up + left): spin right while riding or in the air.
Record: fire + up + right (goofy: fire + down + left): duck and turn right while riding.
Record: fire + down + left (goofy: fire + up + right): spin left.
Record: fire + up + left (goofy: fire + down + right): duck and turn left.
The empty record: do_nothing for every state; every impossible stick value points here.
Low bytes of the 25 text rows of the screen at $5000 (print_char).
High bytes of the 25 text rows as offsets 0-3, added to $50 for the screen and $D8 for colour RAM (print_char).
Bit n for sprite n ($01 ... $80): set bits in the enable, multicolour and x MSB masks. Read from several starting points ($3B3F, $3B40) to reach sprites n+1 and n+2.
sprite_bits + 1: bit n+1, read to set the next sprite's bit with the same index.
sprite_bits + 2: bit n+2.
The inverted bits ($FE ... $7F) to clear sprite n's bit, also read from $3B47 and $3B48.
sprite_clear_bits + 1: the inverted bit of sprite n+1.
sprite_clear_bits + 2: the inverted bit of sprite n+2.
Screen codes of the hex digits 0-F for print_bcd: $30-$39 then 1-6 (A-F).
Terrain handlers for the middle cell under the skater, by type 0-F (apply_terrain $126A).
Terrain handlers for the left and right cells by type: types 0-9 do nothing ($12BC), A-F as for the middle cell.
Map row of each of the 35 flags (0-$FC down the course).
Map column of each flag.
Per flag, the value swapped with the cloth cell when it is knocked down and back when restored (knock_flag, restore_flags).
Per flag, which way it falls: 0 characters $FB/$FC, 1 $FD/$FE.
For the standing flag characters $80-$8A, the character drawn when the flag is down (flag_down_char $163B).
The skull's jaw, characters $EA/$EB: animate_course_chars copies eight bytes from $3C35 + f and eight from $3C3D + f, f = 0 or 1, so the two frames are the same bytes shifted by one row.
The second jaw character's rows (see $3C35).
Flag cloth for character $81, four frames of eight bytes; the frame's bytes are also copied into the middle column of the overlay flag sprite, block $0C ($4301, every third byte).
Flag cloth for character $86, four frames.
Flag cloth for character $87, four frames.
Flag cloth for character $89, four frames.
Pose numbers, one per frame, for every action and fall; each action's list starts at $3CC6 + $3D57,action.
Start of each action's pose list in $3CC6, actions 0-$0E.
Last frame number of each action 0-$0E.
Vertical steps (falls) and pose y offsets (actions) by frame; each action's run starts at $3D75 + $3DEC,action.
Start of each action's run in $3D75.
Horizontal steps of the falls by frame, from $3DFB + $3E41,action (fall_slide).
Start of each fall action's run (0-6) in $3DFB.
Frames per animation frame for each action 0-$0E.
Address of each action's pose directory in the copy of file $1C under the I/O area ($CE00-$D520), words by action 0-$0E; action 0's word is 0 (no action).
High byte of action 0's directory word: 0, since action 0 is no action and is never drawn.
Directory addresses of actions 1-$0E: $CE00, $CEF0, $CEF0, $CFB0, $D088, $D160, $D328, $D358, $D328, $D3D0, $D3D0, $D400, $D448, $D520.

Board sprite offsets for the scripted actions (place_action_board): action 7 x from $3E75 + frame and y from $3E77 + frame (-1/+15, +1/+16); actions 8 and 9 $3E76/$3E78 (+1, +16); $0A-$0E $3E79/$3E7A (+8, +16, less the frame's offset).
Board x offset +1: action 7's second frame (board_offsets + 1) and the fixed x offset of actions 8 and 9 ($2AC7).
Board y offset +15: action 7's first frame, read as $3E77 + frame ($2AEB).
Board y offset +16: action 7's second frame and the fixed y offset of actions 8 and 9 ($2AD1).
Board x offset +8 for the slowing and final actions $0A-$0E ($2B0A).
Board y offset +16 for actions $0A-$0E, less the frame's offset $3F30 ($2B14).
Where each of a sprite's 63 bytes goes when mirrored (copy_pose_shape): 2, 1, 0, 5, 4, 3 ..., swapping the left and right bytes of each row.
Last byte offsets (from $4FC0) of the three bobbing lake characters $F8-$FA, for moving one down.
First byte offsets of the three lake characters, for moving one up.
Which way each lake object moves next (run-time, 0 or 1).
The skull jaw's frame (0/1, toggled).
The flag cloth's frame counter (low two bits used).
Map rows of the four type-C objects for place_overlays (hurdle 1, hurdle 2, the arch on the right, the building): $56, $60, $97, $AA.
Map rows where the objects are checked against $3F08 (terrain_objects): $55, $60, $99, $B7; the hurdles' entries are the ones used for the jump and duck tests.
x of the object overlay sprites, by object.
Sprite bytes for the bar rows of overlay block $0D, hurdle 1 and 2: $00 and $50.
Sprite bytes for the bar rows of block $0E: $00 and $05.
Points for successive jumps over water since the last fall: 5, $20, $40, $40. Nothing stops the index at four: later jumps read $4C, $80, $08, $07, $C3, $37 and zeros from the bytes after it.
Ten bytes nothing reads except as water points past the table's end ($4C $80 $08 $07 $C3 $37 00 00 00): leftovers in the file.
Copy of $D018 taken at start-up by save_video_registers ($1E2C); never read.
Copy of $DD00 (VIC bank) taken at start-up; never read.
Copy of $D021 taken at start-up; never read.
Trick score, low byte (BCD): the points banked during the race. From here to $3F81 init_race clears every byte at the start of each run.
Trick score, high byte (BCD). On the results line it is multiplied by 100 and added to the time score.
Frames left for the *nn* points display on row 1 (set to $50 by show_pending_points).
Points just earned (BCD), added by add_points ($0C4E) and moved on by show_pending_points each frame.
Points being shown as *nn*: the latest batch of new points, added to the trick score when shown; a later batch replaces it on the display.
The facing $3F14 at takeoff, compared on landing: landing the other way round scores 1.
Frame counter of the race clock: six frames make a tenth of a second.
Race clock, tenths of a second (0-9).
Race clock, seconds (BCD, 00-59).
Race clock, minutes (0-9).
Non-zero while the race clock runs: set on the start line (terrain type 9), cleared at the finish.
The fall action playing (1-6; 4 and 5 are the falls forwards and backwards, 6 the splash), 0 when none.
Frame number within the playing action or fall.
x offset of the pose entry being drawn (read_pose_entry), mirrored when the pose is flipped.
y offset of the pose entry being drawn.
The course's fine scroll value for this frame, kept by the scroll band for the course band's timing.
print_bcd keeps the caller's Y here and restores it.
Skater state: 0 riding, 1 in the air, 2 crouching to jump, 3 landing, 4 falling, 5 at the start, 6 past the finish; picks the handler from the control record.
Turn input, -1, 0 or +1: stepped by the left and right handlers, added to the turn accumulator by steer_step.
Sub-counter of the turn input: one step of $3EFA per four frames.
Spin rate, -$20 to +$20: grown by fire + left/right, a half turn when it reaches the end.
Sub-counter of the spin rate.
Heading: 0 straight down the course, signed for left and right, wrapping between $20 and $E0 when the skater turns round.
|heading|, left by steer_step, indexes the speed split table $394F.
Down-course share of the speed for the heading ($394F by |heading|), signed: negative past sideways.
|down_speed_factor|: the loop count of the multiply in update_velocity.
Non-zero while the skater is hidden under a bridge or inside the big pipe.
Collision flag: bounced off a low wall at the side; handled by handle_collisions (bounce_off_wall).
Collision flag: ran into a wall cell (type $A) in the middle under 14 high (hit_low_wall).
Collision flag: a sideways step into a ramp side wall (types 2/3) or a wall; falls (hit_wall_fall).
Non-zero while fire + down holds the skater ducked: needed under hurdle 2, the pipe top and inside the pipe.
Pixels of scroll per one unit of ground rise on a ramp (set_ramp_rate).
The map row under the skater's feet ((scroll + y) / 8, capped), used by the terrain handlers to tell objects apart.
Index (0-34) of the flag being tested, knocked down or restored.
Colour-map byte written with the fallen flag's characters.
Grass and bench slowing: every fifth frame on the ground an extra slow_down.
Grass and bench slowing: slow_down on every other frame.
Random generator state, low byte (random $1E86).
Random generator state, high byte; its low bits also time the random exhortations.
Set by a jump at hurdle 1 or the arch on the right: the skater's sprites are drawn in front of the overlay sprites until landing.
Takeoff flag: set by the jump, cleared when landing begins; holds the airborne pose.
Scroll position at the last ramp step, compared with $25 by terrain_ramp.
